sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Happy New Year, beautiful nerds.
sentences.zh: 新年快乐，可爱的书呆子们。

sentences.en: It is now the impossibly futuristic-sounding 2025,
sentences.zh: 现在是听上去充满未来感的2025年，

sentences.en: and we are ringing in the new year with our 20th edition of Mini Stories,
sentences.zh: 我们将迎来第20届迷你故事特辑，

sentences.en: featuring tales about Cold War neon signs, Japanese fire escapes,
sentences.zh: 其中包含冷战霓虹灯、日本逃生梯的故事，

sentences.en: the marvels of smell-o-vision.
sentences.zh: 以及气味电影的奇妙之处。

sentences.en: But first, we must wake up from our holiday slumber.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我们必须从假日的沉睡中醒来。

sentences.en: Brace yourselves.
sentences.zh: 做好心理准备。

sentences.en: I live in a house with seven other people.
sentences.zh: 我和另外七个人住在一栋房子里。

sentences.en: I'm going to let that sink in for a second.
sentences.zh: 我要让你们消化一下这个事实。

sentences.en: That is a lot of humans under one roof with a lot of different schedules,
sentences.zh: 这么多人在一个屋檐下，有着各种不同的作息时间，

sentences.en: which means a lot of alarms going off anywhere from 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 这意味着从早上6点开始，

sentences.en: to, I don't know, 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 一直到，我不知道，早上10点，会有各种闹钟此起彼伏。

sentences.en: There's the one that's like...
sentences.zh: 其中有一个闹钟是这样的……

sentences.en: But it goes for like an hour because it doesn't actually wake anyone up.
sentences.zh: 但它会响上大约一个小时，因为它实际上谁也叫不醒。

sentences.en: And then the one that really, really gets me is the duck.
sentences.zh: 然后，真正让我崩溃的是那只鸭子。

sentences.en: Wah!
sentences.zh: 嘎！

sentences.en: Wah!
sentences.zh: 嘎！

sentences.en: Wah!
sentences.zh: 嘎！

sentences.en: Wah!
sentences.zh: 嘎！

sentences.en: Now, everyone has their own way of waking up.
sentences.zh: 现在，每个人都有自己醒来的方式。

sentences.en: Personally, I don't really need an alarm because the fear, dread, and obligation of middle age
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我其实不需要闹钟，因为中年人的恐惧、焦虑和责任感

sentences.en: keeps my consciousness right at the edge of alert at all times.
sentences.zh: 时刻让我的意识保持在高度警觉的边缘。

sentences.en: But in my house, this morning chorus of quacks and bird songs exist
sentences.zh: 但在我的家里，之所以每天早晨都有嘎嘎声和鸟鸣声交织的合唱，

sentences.en: because almost everyone sets their alarms early,
sentences.zh: 是因为几乎每个人都把闹钟设得很早，

sentences.en: often much earlier than they actually need to get up.
sentences.zh: 往往比他们实际起床的时间早得多。

sentences.en: And that's because they are building in time to abuse the worst feature of their alarm,
sentences.zh: 那是因为他们在腾出时间来滥用闹钟最糟糕的功能，

sentences.en: a feature so cursed and diabolical, it defeats the very purpose of any alarm.
sentences.zh: 一个如此受诅咒且恶魔般的功能，它违背了任何闹钟的初衷。

sentences.en: I'm talking, of course, about the snooze button.
sentences.zh: 我说的当然是贪睡按钮。

sentences.en: The snooze button is a bad solution to a conundrum that's existed for millennia.
sentences.zh: 贪睡按钮是针对一个存在了数千年的难题的一个糟糕的解决方案。

sentences.en: People need to sleep, but they also have things to do.
sentences.zh: 人们需要睡觉，但他们也有要做的事情。

sentences.en: In ancient Greece, Plato jolted himself out of bed with a system where a set amount of water
sentences.zh: 在古希腊，柏拉图通过一种系统让自己从床上惊醒，该系统是一定量的水

sentences.en: slowly dripped into an airtight pot until the pressure was so high
sentences.zh: 缓慢滴入一个密封罐中，直到压力大到

sentences.en: it would let out a piercing sound, kind of like a teapot.
sentences.zh: 会发出刺耳的声音，有点像茶壶。

sentences.en: And during the Industrial Revolution,
sentences.zh: 在工业革命期间，

sentences.en: some towns had gigantic whistles which summoned workers to the factory.
sentences.zh: 有些城镇有巨大的汽笛，召唤工人们去工厂。

sentences.en: Around the same time, a whole job existed for people who would go around
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时期，曾有专门的一种职业，人们四处走动

sentences.en: knocking on doors and windows to wake people up.
sentences.zh: 敲击门窗来叫醒人们。

sentences.en: But once the alarm clock entered the household with sounds like this and this,
sentences.zh: 但一旦闹钟进入千家万户，发出像这样和那样的声音，

sentences.en: a backlash was inevitable.
sentences.zh: 强烈的反弹就不可避免了。

sentences.en: It was only a matter of time.
sentences.zh: 这只是时间问题。

sentences.en: You can sleep soundly depending upon the snooze alarm clock, the GE Telecron.
sentences.zh: 你可以睡个安稳觉，这取决于贪睡闹钟，通用电气的特克龙（GE Telecron）。

sentences.en: It wakes you each morning and then lets you snooze,
sentences.zh: 它每天早晨叫醒你，然后让你小睡，

sentences.en: continues to wake you just as you choose.
sentences.zh: 正如你所选择的那样，继续叫醒你。

sentences.en: In 1956, GE invented the world's first alarm clock with a snooze button.
sentences.zh: 1956年，通用电气发明了世界上第一个带有贪睡按钮的闹钟。

sentences.en: On top of the clock, there was a big old fat bar labeled snooze.
sentences.zh: 在时钟的顶部，有一个大而粗的杠杆，上面标着“贪睡”。

sentences.en: That's S-N-O-O-Z.
sentences.zh: 也就是 S-N-O-O-Z。

sentences.en: And it could not be missed.
sentences.zh: 而且你绝对不会错过它。

sentences.en: One smack of the clock and presto.
sentences.zh: 只要拍一下时钟，大功告成。

sentences.en: You just bought yourself a little more sleep.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚为自己多争取了一会儿睡眠。

sentences.en: The first snooze alarm clocks were built to let you snooze for 10 to 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 最早的贪睡闹钟旨在让你小睡10到15分钟。

sentences.en: But mass production required some standardization.
sentences.zh: 但大规模生产需要一些标准化。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, a double-digit snooze was too complicated to program into the gears of a clock at scale.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代，要在成规模的时钟齿轮中编程实现两位数的贪睡时间实在是太复杂了。

sentences.en: So GE cut as close as they could with nine minutes.
sentences.zh: 因此，通用电气尽可能接近地选择了九分钟。

sentences.en: A nine-minute snooze was the choice.
sentences.zh: 九分钟的贪睡成为了首选。

sentences.en: After a millennia of trying to get ourselves out of bed at a certain time,
sentences.zh: 在历经数千年试图在特定时间让自己起床之后，

sentences.en: the snooze alarm dared to ask,
sentences.zh: 贪睡闹钟竟敢发问，

sentences.en: Do you really have to get up right now?
sentences.zh: 你真的非得现在就起床吗？

sentences.en: And across the country, people more or less said,
sentences.zh: 全国各地的人们或多或少地回答说：

sentences.en: No, I don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我不用。

sentences.en: The clock was a major hit.
sentences.zh: 这款时钟大获成功。

sentences.en: And as technology improved, a few competitors ended up offering alternatives to the nine-minute snooze,
sentences.zh: 随着技术的改进，一些竞争对手最终为九分钟的贪睡提供了替代方案，

sentences.en: like the West Clock's drowse alarm clock.
sentences.zh: 比如西方钟表公司的打盹闹钟。

sentences.en: Want five minutes more sleep or 10?
sentences.zh: 想要再睡五分钟还是十分钟？

sentences.en: The West Clock's alarm clock gave people the option of snoozing two different amounts of time,
sentences.zh: 西方钟表公司的闹钟让人们可以选择两种不同的贪睡时间，

sentences.en: depending on if you hit the drowse button on the left side or the right side.
sentences.zh: 这取决于你按下的是左侧还是右侧的打盹按钮。

sentences.en: Gee, I could use 10 minutes this time.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这次我能用上十分钟。

sentences.en: Man, you just can't oversleep with this new West Clock.
sentences.zh: 天啊，有了这个新西方时钟，你绝对不会睡过头。

sentences.en: But the drowse button didn't have that sweet, sweet simplicity.
sentences.zh: 但打盹按钮却没有那种美妙而纯粹的简单性。

sentences.en: Nobody wants to wake up and think about how much longer they want to sleep.
sentences.zh: 没有人醒来后还想去琢磨自己到底想多睡多久。

sentences.en: People just want to sleep more.
sentences.zh: 人们只是想多睡一会儿。

sentences.en: And the snooze button gave us that.
sentences.zh: 而贪睡按钮给了我们这一点。

sentences.en: Or at least that's what we thought.
sentences.zh: 或者至少我们是这么认为的。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that many of our phones are still factory preset to snooze for nine minutes,
sentences.zh: 尽管我们的许多手机出厂默认设置仍然是贪睡九分钟，

sentences.en: today we all know deep down that the snooze button doesn't really give us meaningful sleep.
sentences.zh: 但今天我们内心深处都知道，贪睡按钮并不能真正给我们带来有意义的睡眠。

sentences.en: And it also doesn't let us rise.
sentences.zh: 它也不能让我们真正振作起来。

sentences.en: Instead, it catches us at our weakest moment,
sentences.zh: 相反，它在我们最薄弱的时刻抓住了我们，

sentences.en: when we are least capable of making decisions,
sentences.zh: 在我们最没有能力做决定的时刻，

sentences.en: when it's far easier to slap a button than to put two feet on the ground.
sentences.zh: 拍一下按钮比把双脚着地要容易得多。

sentences.en: In the end, the key to waking up might just rest in not giving yourself any other options.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，起床的秘诀可能就在于不给自己留下任何其他选择。

sentences.en: And the key to more sleep?
sentences.zh: 那么睡得更多的秘诀呢？

sentences.en: Well, let me know when someone figures that out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，等有人弄明白了请告诉我。

sentences.en: I'm here with 99PI editor Kelly Prime for a rare appearance on mic.
sentences.zh: 我和99PI的编辑凯利·普莱姆（Kelly Prime）一起，进行了一次罕见的麦克风出场。

sentences.en: So, Kelly, what do you have for me today?
sentences.zh: 那么，凯利，你今天给我带来了什么？

sentences.en: Hi, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嗨，罗曼。

sentences.en: So, I want you to imagine this very classic Americana neon scene.
sentences.zh: 我想让你想象一下这种非常经典的美国风情霓虹灯场景。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, like, if you imagine pictures of Broadway or vintage Las Vegas,
sentences.zh: 所以，就像，如果你想象百老汇的照片或复古的拉斯维加斯，

sentences.en: like, the street just lit up with signs sort of competing for your attention.
sentences.zh: 就像，街道上灯火辉煌，各种招牌仿佛在争夺你的注意力。

sentences.en: Can you picture that?
sentences.zh: 你能想象那个画面吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely, I can picture that.
sentences.zh: 当然，我能想象得到。

sentences.en: Okay, great, because that's not what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 好的，太好了，因为我说的不是那个。

sentences.en: Okay, well, I'll erase that from my mind.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我把它从脑子里删掉。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's the neon that you and I are probably more familiar with.
sentences.zh: 那是你和我可能更熟悉的霓虹灯。

sentences.en: But I want to tell you a story about a different neon aesthetic.
sentences.zh: 但我想给你讲一个关于不同霓虹灯美学的故事。

sentences.en: It's one that was created in the Eastern Bloc, right in the middle of the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 它是在东欧集团创造的，正值冷战时期。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And they basically took that flashy, commercial Americana style of neon,
sentences.zh: 他们基本上采用了那种浮夸、商业化的美国霓虹灯风格，

sentences.en: and they twisted it to make this new socialist style that's completely unique to this specific place
sentences.zh: 并对其进行了扭曲，创造出这种全新的社会主义风格，完全独特于这个特定的地方

sentences.en: at this specific moment of history.
sentences.zh: 以及历史上的这个特定时刻。

sentences.en: Huh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哈，好吧。

sentences.en: Tell me more about it.
sentences.zh: 跟我多讲讲。

sentences.en: So, the story starts in the mid-50s, about a decade into communism in the Eastern Bloc.
sentences.zh: 所以，故事始于50年代中期，也就是东欧共产主义开始大约十年后。

sentences.en: At this point, people were starting to push back, to rebel.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，人们开始反抗，开始叛逆。

sentences.en: And so, Soviet leaders got together, and they were like,
sentences.zh: 于是，苏联领导人聚在一起，他们当时想的是，

sentences.en: we have to work out a plan to quell some of this political unreSt.
sentences.zh: 我们必须制定一个计划来平息一些政治动荡。

sentences.en: And their plan was basically neon.
sentences.zh: 他们的计划基本上就是霓虹灯。

sentences.en: It was called neonization.
sentences.zh: 这被称为霓虹化。

sentences.en: It was the state-sponsored program.
sentences.zh: 这是一个国家资助的项目。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm in.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我加入。

sentences.en: Tell me more.
sentences.zh: 多告诉我一些。

sentences.en: Okay, neonization was a government program meant to push the idea of a brighter future.
sentences.zh: 好的，霓虹化是一个旨在推行光明未来的政府项目。

sentences.en: Since this is your first time recording with me, I will allow you that one once.
sentences.zh: 既然这是你第一次和我一起录音，我就破例允许你这一次。

sentences.en: But another one of those, and I'm pulling the plug.
sentences.zh: 但如果还有下一次，我就要拔掉电源了。

sentences.en: We'll see.
sentences.zh: 咱们走着瞧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The concept was like, okay, things are bleak, we get that.
sentences.zh: 这个概念就像是，好吧，情况很黯淡，我们懂的。

sentences.en: But shh, don't even worry about it.
sentences.zh: 但是嘘，甚至不用担心这个。

sentences.en: Look at these lights.
sentences.zh: 看看这些灯光。

sentences.en: So, what they decided to do was change the landscape,
sentences.zh: 所以，他们决定做的是改变风景，

sentences.en: turn things around, brighten up everything.
sentences.zh: 扭转局面，照亮一切。

sentences.en: That's David Hill.
sentences.zh: 那是大卫·希尔（David Hill）。

sentences.en: He's the director of the Neon Museum in Warsaw,
sentences.zh: 他是华沙霓虹灯博物馆的馆长，

sentences.en: which is dedicated to documenting and preserving Cold War-era neon signs.
sentences.zh: 该博物馆致力于记录和保护冷战时期的霓虹灯招牌。

sentences.en: The proponents certainly argued, this will placate the public.
sentences.zh: 支持者当然辩称，这会安抚公众。

sentences.en: This will bamboozle them.
sentences.zh: 这会迷惑他们。

sentences.en: This will make people happy again.
sentences.zh: 这会让人们再次快乐起来。

sentences.en: So, rather than provide things, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，与其提供各种东西，你知道的，

sentences.en: substantive things in their lives to actually make people happy,
sentences.zh: 生活中真正能让人快乐的实质性东西，

sentences.en: they just decided to put lights in front of them.
sentences.zh: 他们只是决定在人们面前放一些灯光。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, great use of resources.
sentences.zh: 是啊，真是对资源的极好利用。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And so, why neon specifically?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么偏偏是霓虹灯？

sentences.en: Why not murals or, you know, I don't know, anything else?
sentences.zh: 为什么不是壁画，或者，你知道的，其他任何东西？

sentences.en: So, the thing is that Eastern Europe actually had a history with neon,
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的，东欧其实有着霓虹灯的历史，

sentences.en: and this was especially true of Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 华沙尤其如此。

sentences.en: So, before World War II,
sentences.zh: 所以，在二战之前，

sentences.en: Warsaw had been just like another modern European capital
sentences.zh: 华沙就像另一个现代的欧洲首都一样，

sentences.en: with everything that entailed, including bright, shiny lights.
sentences.zh: 具备与之俱来的一切，包括明亮闪耀的灯光。

sentences.en: It was a shimmering pearl.
sentences.zh: 它是一颗璀璨的明珠。

sentences.en: It was very famous for its neon signs from 1926 onwards.
sentences.zh: 从1926年起，它就以霓虹灯招牌而闻名遐迩。

sentences.en: So, it had this connection to neon.
sentences.zh: 所以它与霓虹灯有着这种联系。

sentences.en: But the war just basically destroyed all of them.
sentences.zh: 但战争基本上摧毁了所有这些。

sentences.en: As you can imagine, these very delicate glass tubes would not fare well
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，这些非常脆弱的玻璃管在所有发生的轰炸中

sentences.en: in all the bombings that happened.
sentences.zh: 是不会有好下场的。

sentences.en: But even though they were gone, people in Warsaw still had a really positive association with them.
sentences.zh: 但尽管它们消失了，华沙的人们仍然对它们有着非常积极的联想。

sentences.en: It really represented modernity and just generally prosperity, like before things were destroyed.
sentences.zh: 它确实代表了现代感和普遍的繁荣，就像事物被破坏之前那样。

sentences.en: So, the socialist government knew that,
sentences.zh: 所以，社会主义政府深知这一点，

sentences.en: and they figured they could sort of leverage that association to foster goodwill towards the current regime.
sentences.zh: 他们认为可以利用这种联系来培养人们对当前政权的善意。

sentences.en: So, the communist government came up with this plan to neonize the city to make everyone happy.
sentences.zh: 因此，共产党政府提出了这个让城市充满霓虹灯的计划，旨在让每个人都开心。

sentences.en: So, what's step one in this process?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个过程的第一步是什么？

sentences.en: Like, how do they start?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们是怎么开始的？

sentences.en: So, one of the first things the government did was to hire some of the best artists in the nation.
sentences.zh: 所以，政府做的第一件事之一就是聘请国内一些最优秀的艺术家。

sentences.en: And like, some of these people actually were already talented neon artists and electricians,
sentences.zh: 而且其中有些人实际上已经是很有天赋的霓虹灯艺术家和电工了，

sentences.en: but many of them weren't.
sentences.zh: 但他们当中很多人并不是。

sentences.en: Like, these were groundbreaking visual artists who were used to working on paper and canvas.
sentences.zh: 比如，这些是具有开创性的视觉艺术家，他们习惯于在纸张和画布上创作。

sentences.en: They didn't necessarily have any pre-existing experience working with neon.
sentences.zh: 他们不一定有任何预先使用霓虹灯创作的经验。

sentences.en: So, the only thing that was really limiting their imagination was the bounds of the material.
sentences.zh: 所以，唯一真正限制他们想象力的就是材料本身的边界。

sentences.en: They would just have a piece of cardboard and just draw lines all over it.
sentences.zh: 他们会拿出一张硬纸板，在上面到处画线。

sentences.en: And then later realize, well, that's not really possible.
sentences.zh: 然后后来才意识到，嗯，这其实是不可能的。

sentences.en: We can't make that.
sentences.zh: 我们做不出那种效果。

sentences.en: It's too zigzaggy or, you know, whatever the restrictions were.
sentences.zh: 它的折线太多了，你知道的，不管有什么限制。

sentences.en: Okay, so, given that, given that their imagination is sort of wild and is unfettered by the constraints of neon,
sentences.zh: 好吧，鉴于此，鉴于他们的想象力有点天马行空，且不受霓虹灯限制的约束，

sentences.en: but there are actual physical constraints of building something in neon,
sentences.zh: 但用霓虹灯建造东西确实存在物理限制，

sentences.en: what exactly did the artists end up making?
sentences.zh: 艺术家们最终到底创作出了什么？

sentences.en: I'm so glad you asked because I've been very into these since I discovered them.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你问起这个，因为自从我发现它们以来，我就对这些东西非常着迷。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And I think the best way to go about it is just to show you some examples.
sentences.zh: 我想最好的方法就是向你展示一些例子。

sentences.en: So, the first one I'm about to ask you to look at was made to decorate a flower shop.
sentences.zh: 所以，我要让你看的第一个是为装饰一家花店而制作的。

sentences.en: So, just describe what you're seeing here.
sentences.zh: 那么，请描述一下你在这里看到了什么。

sentences.en: So, I'm seeing very bright neon and it's a green kind of vine, lots of flowers of a couple of different colors.
sentences.zh: 我看到非常明亮的霓虹灯，它是一种绿色的藤蔓，还有许多不同颜色的花朵。

sentences.en: And the flower petals, like, they're not uniform.
sentences.zh: 花瓣看起来并不统一。

sentences.en: They're like, they're kind of, they're kind of scribbly.
sentences.zh: 它们有点像，有点像涂鸦出来的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're like scribbly.
sentences.zh: 它们就像涂鸦一样。

sentences.en: It looks like a sketch pad, like someone has been doodling, but on an entire building with neon.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像一个素描本，就像有人在涂鸦，但却是在一整栋建筑上用霓虹灯涂鸦。

sentences.en: This was designed by a graphic artist, Zofia Kostetska, now Kosciupska.
sentences.zh: 这是由平面艺术家佐菲娅·科斯泰茨卡（现姓科斯修普斯卡）设计的。

sentences.en: So, she created this as a young graphic designer for a pavilion that sold basically carnations and roses.
sentences.zh: 所以，她作为一名年轻的平面设计师，为一家主要出售康乃馨和玫瑰的展馆创作了这件作品。

sentences.en: Nothing fancy there, except the building was covered in butterflies and flowers and grass.
sentences.zh: 那里没有什么特别fancy的东西，只不过建筑上布满了蝴蝶、花朵和青草。

sentences.en: It was enormous.
sentences.zh: 它非常巨大。

sentences.en: It went on for meters.
sentences.zh: 绵延数米。

sentences.en: We're talking 20, 30 meters.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是20米、30米。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, these are big.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都很大。

sentences.en: They're huge.
sentences.zh: 它们巨大无比。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: These are huge.
sentences.zh: 这些太大了。

sentences.en: 20, 30 meters, that's 100 feet of squiggly flowers.
sentences.zh: 20、30米，那就是100英尺蜿蜒曲折的花朵。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: It's crazy.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, the next one I want to show you is actually, the scale is not the same, but it is one of my favorites.
sentences.zh: 我想向你展示的下一个作品，其实规模没有那么大，但它是我最喜欢的作品之一。

sentences.en: It's a pink mermaid and she's holding up a sword and shield, which is like the mermaid with the sword and shield is the symbol of the city of Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 那是一只粉红色的美人鱼，她举着剑和盾，就像手持剑和盾的美人鱼是华沙市的象征一样。

sentences.en: And she's hovering over an open book.
sentences.zh: 她盘旋在一本翻开的书上方。

sentences.en: Wherever you saw this beautiful pink mermaid sitting on an open book, she would denote your public library.
sentences.zh: 无论你在哪里看到这只美丽粉红的美人鱼坐在翻开的书上，她就代表着你的公共图书馆。

sentences.en: So, Bibliotheca Publiczno.
sentences.zh: 也就是华沙公共图书馆。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So, you'd see this symbol all over the place in Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 所以你在华沙到处都能看到这个标志。

sentences.en: That's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: This thing is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这东西太美了。

sentences.en: It's hard to imagine neon over municipal buildings.
sentences.zh: 很难想象市政建筑上会装满霓虹灯。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I was in Saugerties, New York, like literally yesterday, and there was a pink neon framing of this old industrial bridge.
sentences.zh: 我 буквально昨天（字面意思：就在昨天）还在纽约索格蒂斯，那里有一个用粉红霓虹灯勾勒轮廓的老工业桥梁。

sentences.en: And I was just like mesmerized by that thing.
sentences.zh: 我当时简直被那东西迷住了。

sentences.en: And just like that sort of juxtaposition of neon and, you know, just like kind of pretty mundane municipal design and decay was like lovely.
sentences.zh: 霓虹灯与那种相当平淡的市政设计和破败景象的结合，简直太美妙了。

sentences.en: It was a revelation to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是一个启示。

sentences.en: I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I want more of that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想看更多这样的东西。

sentences.en: And that was like very much the thing here, like very much the thing.
sentences.zh: 这里的确非常盛行这种风格，可以说是无处不在。

sentences.en: So, by the late 60s, Warsaw had hundreds of thousands of these signs across the city.
sentences.zh: 因此，到60年代末，华沙全市有几十万个这样的招牌。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But what's really striking to me is the fact that all of these neon signs had this cohesiveness to them.
sentences.zh: 但真正让我惊叹的是，所有这些霓虹灯招牌都具有如此高的整体协调性。

sentences.en: You know, if you cast your mind to that, again, American scene of a street covered in neon, what you're going to see is a big sort of mishmash of color.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你回想一下美国那种霓虹灯密布的街道场景，你会发现那是一种五颜六色的大杂烩。

sentences.en: But in Poland, that was not at all the case.
sentences.zh: 但在波兰，情况完全不是这样。

sentences.en: We're looking at something as a very well thought out, coherent project.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是一个经过深思熟虑、前后连贯的项目。

sentences.en: And I think that delivered a slightly different aesthetic, a different feeling.
sentences.zh: 我认为这带来了一种略有不同的美学，一种不同的感觉。

sentences.en: As if, my God, the city is a city of neon.
sentences.zh: 仿佛，天哪，这座城市是一座霓虹之城。

sentences.en: It's a city of light.
sentences.zh: 这是一座光之城。

sentences.en: And it all seems to work together.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切似乎都融为一体。

sentences.en: It all seems to be harmonious.
sentences.zh: 这一切似乎都那么和谐。

sentences.en: And a big reason for that is the fact that this neonization process was run by the state.
sentences.zh: 其中一个重大原因在于，这种霓虹化过程是由国家主导的。

sentences.en: There was actually a central body that commissioned and signed off on every single sign.
sentences.zh: 实际上有一个中央机构负责委托并批准每一个招牌。

sentences.en: You'd think they'd have better things to do.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得他们有更重要的事情要做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, I guess not.
sentences.zh: 不，我想并没有。

sentences.en: And all these signs were specifically designed to complement each other.
sentences.zh: 所有这些招牌都是专门设计来相辅相成的。

sentences.en: So no one piece was approved unless it fit into the style of the whole.
sentences.zh: 所以，除非符合整体风格，否则任何一件作品都不会被批准。

sentences.en: You can see how seriously the authorities took this in that eventually the chief city architect's title was abolished and it became the chief city graphic designer.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出当局对这件事有多认真，以至于后来首席城市建筑师的头衔被废除了，取而代之的是首席城市平面设计师。

sentences.en: So there was less importance on architecture and more placed on neonization and the urban aesthetic, the design.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们不再那么重视建筑，而是更加重视霓虹化、城市美学和设计。

sentences.en: So after all this neonization, Warsaw is covered in neon.
sentences.zh: 所以在经历了这一切霓虹化之后，华沙到处都是霓虹灯。

sentences.en: But did their ultimate goal actually bear fruit?
sentences.zh: 但他们的最终目标真的见效了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, were people actually, you know, happier?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们真的，你知道的，更快乐了吗？

sentences.en: Did they convince the people of Poland that everything was OK?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有让波兰人民相信一切都好？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, it's hard to say how people in Poland felt about neonization in general.
sentences.zh: 首先，很难说波兰人民对整体的霓虹化作何感想。

sentences.en: Certainly the signs were really beautiful.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些招牌真的很美。

sentences.en: And it's easy to appreciate their beauty.
sentences.zh: 欣赏它们的美并不难。

sentences.en: But it's also safe to say that this tricked exactly no one into thinking that, you know, life under communism was really great.
sentences.zh: 但也可以肯定的是，这绝对没有蒙骗任何人去相信，你知道的，共产主义下的生活真的很美好。

sentences.en: By the early 80s, things had in fact gotten so bad that the socialist government instituted martial law.
sentences.zh: 到80年代初，情况实际上已经变得如此糟糕，以至于社会主义政府实行了军事管制。

sentences.en: And that really took a toll on Warsaw's neons.
sentences.zh: 这确实对华沙的霓虹灯造成了打击。

sentences.en: These neon signs were switched off.
sentences.zh: 这些霓虹灯招牌被关闭了。

sentences.en: The authorities said, well, you don't need them.
sentences.zh: 当局说，好吧，你们不需要它们。

sentences.en: You know, you're under you're under house arreSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你们正在被软禁。

sentences.en: Why would you want to go out in the evening?
sentences.zh: 为什么还要在晚上出门？

sentences.en: So they were basically switched off.
sentences.zh: 所以它们基本上都被关闭了。

sentences.en: And they were really the first rather obvious victims of this new political revolution that brought in democracy.
sentences.zh: 它们确实成为了这场带来民主的新政治革命的最初、相当明显的牺牲品。

sentences.en: And what happened next, you probably know, communism in the Eastern Bloc didn't laSt.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么，你大概也知道，东欧的共产主义并没有持续下去。

sentences.en: In 1989, Poland's communist state was officially replaced by a new democratic government.
sentences.zh: 1989年，波兰的共产主义国家正式被一个新的民主政府取代。

sentences.en: And when that happened, that was really the end for Warsaw's neons.
sentences.zh: 当这一切发生时，华沙的霓虹灯也真正走到了尽头。

sentences.en: The new democratic Polish government looked at the symbols from this period of occupation as they saw it.
sentences.zh: 新的民主波兰政府将这个占领时期的象征（他们眼中的象征）视作眼中钉。

sentences.en: And neon was the obvious target.
sentences.zh: 霓虹灯自然成为了众矢之的。

sentences.en: And so they set about destroying as many neon signs as they could in what they called the Great Recycling Scheme, rather quaintly.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们开始着手摧毁尽可能多的霓虹灯招牌，用他们颇有些田园诗般委婉的说法，这叫“伟大回收计划”。

sentences.en: And we lost so many, so many neons.
sentences.zh: 我们失去了太多的霓虹灯。

sentences.en: Wow, the Great Recycling Scheme is quite a euphemism.
sentences.zh: 哇，“伟大回收计划”真是一个绝妙的委婉说法。

sentences.en: Yeah, people were paid to go out into the city, find the neon signs and destroy them.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们花钱去城里寻找霓虹灯招牌并将其销毁。

sentences.en: So are any of the original signs left up?
sentences.zh: 那么，原有的招牌还剩下一些吗？

sentences.en: I mean, those pictures you showed me, are those contemporary or were all the signs destroyed?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你展示的那些照片是当代的，还是所有的招牌都被毁了？

sentences.en: So those pictures I showed you are contemporary.
sentences.zh: 我向你展示的那些照片是当代的。

sentences.en: Those are photos of some of the few signs that did manage to survive all this time.
sentences.zh: 那些是少数历经风雨幸存下来的霓虹灯招牌的照片。

sentences.en: But most of Warsaw's neons were either broken or taken down.
sentences.zh: 但华沙大部分的霓虹灯要么被砸坏，要么被拆除了。

sentences.en: And eventually the remnants of neonization just kind of faded into the backdrop of the city rather than being what they once were, which is, you know, a focal point of it.
sentences.zh: 最终，霓虹化的遗迹逐渐淡入了城市的背景中，而不再像以前那样成为城市的核心焦点。

sentences.en: But I will say that in the last 20 or so years, there has been renewed interest among the residents of Warsaw in those signs and their history.
sentences.zh: 但我要说的是，在过去的20年左右里，华沙居民对这些招牌及其历史重新燃起了兴趣。

sentences.en: I do have some, you know, some really good news.
sentences.zh: 我确实有一些，你知道的，非常好的消息。

sentences.en: And that is that Warsaw is undergoing a bit of a renaissance.
sentences.zh: 那就是华沙正在经历某种复兴。

sentences.en: Neonization has returned.
sentences.zh: 霓虹化又回来了。

sentences.en: Today, people come from around the world to see what's left of Warsaw's neons.
sentences.zh: 今天，人们从世界各地赶来参观华沙残存的霓虹灯。

sentences.en: And David says that there are now new neon signs all over Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 大卫说现在华沙到处都有新的霓虹灯招牌。

sentences.en: And some of them are directly referencing the work of Poland's great neon artists.
sentences.zh: 其中一些直接借鉴了波兰伟大霓虹灯艺术家的作品。

sentences.en: You see these fantastic places that young people hang out.
sentences.zh: 你看到年轻人聚在一起的这些奇妙地方。

sentences.en: And you look and you think, I've seen that before.
sentences.zh: 当你看着它们时会想，我以前见过这个。

sentences.en: That's a neon design by Jan Moharski, you know, this famous neonizer and Polish poster artiSt.
sentences.zh: 那是扬·莫哈尔斯基设计的霓虹灯，你知道的，这位著名的霓虹灯设计师和波兰海报艺术家。

sentences.en: And there it is on the streets of Warsaw, reinvented for the modern age, reinvented for the young people.
sentences.zh: 它就这样出现在华沙的街头，为现代重新演绎，为年轻人重新演绎。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Kelly.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，凯利。

sentences.en: Thanks, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: And if you'd like to see some examples of these Polish neon signs, we'll have some pictures on the website.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看这些波兰霓虹灯招牌的例子，我们的网站上会有一些照片。

sentences.en: Coming up, our digital director, Kurt Kolstad, figures out how to escape from a burning building in Japan.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们的数字总监库尔特·科尔斯特ad（Kurt Kolstad）将为大家演示如何在日本从着火的建筑中逃生。

sentences.en: News you can use.
sentences.zh: 实用新闻。

sentences.en: And our pal, Gillian Jacobs, talks to us about movies you can smell.
sentences.zh: 我们的朋友吉莉安·雅各布斯将跟我们聊聊可以闻到气味的电影。

sentences.en: That's after the break.
sentences.zh: 广告之后马上回来。

sentences.en: We are back with digital director, Kurt Kolstad.
sentences.zh: 我们和数字总监库尔特·科尔斯特ad回来了。

sentences.en: Kurt, what do you have for us?
sentences.zh: 库尔特，你给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I wanted to tell you about this small design element that I first encountered in Tokyo.
sentences.zh: 我想和大家聊聊我在东京第一次遇到这个小型设计元素。

sentences.en: I was walking around and I started to notice these red stickers that were shaped like perfect equilateral triangles and stuck to the windows of a bunch of different buildings.
sentences.zh: 我在四处闲逛时，开始注意到一些红色的贴纸，它们呈完美的等边三角形形状，贴在许多不同建筑的窗户上。

sentences.en: Here's a picture to show you what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 这是一张照片，向你展示我在说什么。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's see.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们看看。

sentences.en: Yes, it's a red triangle, the tip pointing down, and it's centered right in the middle of every window that I see.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个红色的三角形，尖端朝下，正好居中在我看到的每一个窗户的中间。

sentences.en: Like, it doesn't seem accidental or put on by the people, you know, haphazardly on the inside.
sentences.zh: 看起来不像是偶然的，也不是人们在里面随随便便贴上去的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's a certain consistency to it.
sentences.zh: 它具有某种一致性。

sentences.en: There's like one upside down red triangle every couple of windows.
sentences.zh: 每隔几扇窗户就有一个倒置的红色三角形。

sentences.en: And then, you know, once I noticed them, I started to see these stickers everywhere, not just in Tokyo, but then later in Osaka and Kobe and Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，一旦我注意到它们，我开始到处看到这些贴纸，不仅在东京，后来还在大阪、神户和京都。

sentences.en: You know, now that I've seen these pictures, I have to admit, I didn't see these when I was in Japan.
sentences.zh: 既然我已经看到了这些照片，我必须承认，我在日本时并没有注意到这些。

sentences.en: So what's up with all these stickers?
sentences.zh: 那么这些贴纸是怎么回事？

sentences.en: So they're called fire department access stickers.
sentences.zh: 它们被称为消防部门出入贴纸。

sentences.en: And you shouldn't feel too bad about missing them.
sentences.zh: 你没注意到也不用觉得太糟糕。

sentences.en: It really helped that I had one smack dab in the middle of my first hotel room window in Tokyo.
sentences.zh: 我在东京入住的第一家酒店的窗户正中央就贴着一个，这确实帮了大忙。

sentences.en: So I did some research and I found out that in an emergency, the red triangles indicate to firefighters where to lean their ladders.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了一些研究，发现在紧急情况下，红色的三角形向消防员指示了他们应该把梯子靠在哪里。

sentences.en: And then on the inside, they have explanatory text that tells people in the building where they should go and expect to find rescue.
sentences.zh: 然后在里面，它们有解释性的文字，告诉大楼里的人他们应该去哪里以及预期在哪里找到救援。

sentences.en: Do the triangles indicate that the windows are somehow different or that they're just the gathering point of a rescuer meeting rescuee?
sentences.zh: 三角形是表明窗户有什么不同，还是它们只是救援人员和被救援人员会合的地点？

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: So I looked into that and some of what I read indicated that these windows could be opened more easily, like either by firefighters from the outside or people from the inside.
sentences.zh: 所以我查了一下，我读到的一些内容表明这些窗户可以更容易地打开，比如从外面由消防员打开，或者从里面由人们打开。

sentences.en: And one account indicated that they might be built out of more breakable glass, too, so that like you can shatter them in an emergency.
sentences.zh: 还有一个说法指出它们也可能是用更容易破碎的玻璃建造的，这样你就可以在紧急情况下把它们打碎。

sentences.en: And then I noticed under my window in my hotel room that there was this metal stick, which clearly wasn't there to open the window.
sentences.zh: 然后我注意到我的酒店房间窗户下面有一根金属棍，这显然不是用来开窗的。

sentences.en: And I got to wondering, like, is that so that I can smash the window?
sentences.zh: 我开始纳闷，比如说，那是为了让我砸碎窗户吗？

sentences.en: And I confess I did not test the theory.
sentences.zh: 我承认我没有测试过这个理论。

sentences.en: And so I cannot confirm if that's why the stick was there.
sentences.zh: 所以我无法确认这是否就是那根棍子在那里的原因。

sentences.en: Well, regardless of whether these arrows are indicators of any structural or physical difference about these windows,
sentences.zh: 嗯，不管这些箭头是否代表这些窗户在结构或物理上有任何不同，

sentences.en: this is a place where you can go to get out of the building in an emergency.
sentences.zh: 这里是一个你在紧急情况下可以去逃离大楼的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: It's a meeting point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个集合点。

sentences.en: I guess I'm just kind of surprised that I missed these stickers.
sentences.zh: 我想我只是有点惊讶我竟然错过了这些贴纸。

sentences.en: Like, are they only on certain kinds of buildings or are they just all kind of high up?
sentences.zh: 比如说，它们只在某些类型的建筑上，还是它们只是都在比较高的地方？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, you're on the right track there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，你的方向是对的。

sentences.en: Height is the key determinant, because if you think about it, like smaller buildings, including houses that only have a story or two, obviously wouldn't need these at all.
sentences.zh: 高度是关键决定因素，因为如果你想想看，比如较小的建筑，包括只有一两层楼的房屋，显然根本不需要这些。

sentences.en: And on taller buildings, they'd only be needed within a certain height range, because, of course, if a window is too high to be reached by a firefighter ladder,
sentences.zh: 而在较高的建筑上，它们只在一定的高度范围内需要，因为当然，如果一窗户太高，消防员的梯子够不着，

sentences.en: it would be dark to encourage people to congregate there, frankly.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，如果那样的话，把它们设在那里鼓励人们聚集就会显得很不合理。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: There's only a narrow band where these are functional.
sentences.zh: 只有在一个狭窄的区间内这些才起作用。

sentences.en: They have to be high enough that you wouldn't just get out by yourself on the first floor or second floor,
sentences.zh: 它们必须足够高，以至于你不会在一楼或二楼自己就能直接逃出去，

sentences.en: but low enough that it'd be possible for a firefighter's ladder to reach you.
sentences.zh: 但又必须足够低，以便消防员的梯子能够够到你。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: And from the regulation accounts that I was reading, of course, in translation and secondary sources, it appears that it's about 100 feet where these things cap out.
sentences.zh: 从我读到的规章记录来看，当然是通过翻译和二手资料，看起来这些东西的极限大约是100英尺。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's the reason why I missed them, because it's within 20 feet to 100 feet.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是我错过它们的原因，因为它们在20英尺到100英尺之间。

sentences.en: Totally, and they're really, I mean, quite small, so unless you're looking for them, they're easy to miss, too, right?
sentences.zh: 完全同意，而且它们真的，我是说，相当小，所以除非你在找它们，否则也很容易错过，对吧？

sentences.en: And, you know, this actually all kind of led me back to this little journey of discovery that I took when we first met, which was over a decade ago now, if you can believe it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这实际上让我回想起了我们刚认识时我经历的那段小小探索之旅，如果你能相信的话，那已经是十多年前的事了。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: It's been a while.
sentences.zh: 已经过去一段时间了。

sentences.en: I can't imagine the show before you, so it's one of those things.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象没有你的节目会是什么样，所以就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: So what did it remind you of, though?
sentences.zh: 那它让你想起了什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, we had this lunch together in Oakland, and we were walking around, and you pointed out this little black box next to a building entrance, and then another, and another,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在奥克兰一起吃了午饭，我们在到处走，你指着大楼入口旁边的一个小黑盒子，然后又是一个，再一个，

sentences.en: and so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: And they all had these little red reflective stripes.
sentences.zh: 它们都有这些小小的红色反光条纹。

sentences.en: And those are, of course, Knox boxes, which we've talked about a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 当然，那些就是诺克斯箱，我们已经讨论过好几次了。

sentences.en: And if you don't remember those episodes or didn't read the book that Kurt and I co-authored, those contain a set of keys for the building,
sentences.zh: 如果你不记得那些节目，或者没有读过我和库尔特合著的那本书，那些箱子里装着大楼的一套钥匙，

sentences.en: and then all those Knox boxes are held by firefighters.
sentences.zh: 然后所有这些诺克斯箱都由消防员保管。

sentences.en: So if there is a crisis, they can open up this box, therefore have all the keys to the building, and they can get in and out more easily.
sentences.zh: 所以如果发生危机，他们可以打开这个箱子，从而拥有大楼的所有钥匙，他们就可以更轻松地进出。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: And so you were there for me 10 years ago, drawing my attention to something, and then filling in the backstory.
sentences.zh: 所以10年你在那里，让我注意到某些东西，然后补充了背景故事。

sentences.en: So this is me returning the favor.
sentences.zh: 所以现在轮到我回报了。

sentences.en: Well, that was fun, Kurt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那很有趣，库尔特。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: Up next is actor and frequent 9iMPI contributor Gillian Jacobs.
sentences.zh: 接下来是演员兼9pi频密嘉宾吉莉安·雅各布斯。

sentences.en: Hey, Gillian.
sentences.zh: 嘿，吉莉安。

sentences.en: Welcome back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me, Roman.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我，罗曼。

sentences.en: It's great to have you back.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你回来。

sentences.en: So what do you have for us today?
sentences.zh: 那么今天你给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I wanted to talk about a very particular and peculiar movie.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想聊一部非常特别且奇特的电影。

sentences.en: Roman, have you ever seen the film Scent of Mystery?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你你看过电影《神秘的香味》吗？

sentences.en: No, but I like the way you say Scent of Mystery.
sentences.zh: 没有，但我喜欢你念《神秘的香味》这个名字的方式。

sentences.en: I feel like it can only be said like that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它只能那样念。

sentences.en: So tell me more about Scent of Mystery.
sentences.zh: 所以跟我多讲讲《神秘的香味》吧。

sentences.en: Well, no judgment for never having heard of it, because it's a very obscure movie from 1960.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于没听说过它不用评判，因为它是一部1960年非常冷门的电影。

sentences.en: But as you may be able to deduce, it is a mystery film about a mysterious woman in danger.
sentences.zh: 但正如你可能推断的那样，这是一部关于一个处于危险中的神秘女性的神秘电影。

sentences.en: It has Peter Lorre, wine barrels, Spain, bad Spanish.
sentences.zh: 它有彼得·洛雷、酒桶、西班牙语、糟糕的西班牙语。

sentences.en: The reason I want to talk to you about it today is because my friend Joan saw it when it first came out in theaters
sentences.zh: 我想今天跟你聊它的原因是因为我的朋友琼在它刚在影院上映时看过它，

sentences.en: and is still talking about it because of something unique about Scent of Mystery.
sentences.zh: 并且至今还在谈论它，因为《神秘的香味》有一个独特之处。

sentences.en: So what do you remember about that day and about the movie?
sentences.zh: 那么你对那天和那部电影有什么记忆？

sentences.en: Okay, so much about the movie.
sentences.zh: 好吧，关于这部电影的记忆太多了。

sentences.en: I think we got popcorn because, you know, this was a big event for us to go downtown.
sentences.zh: 我想我们买了爆米花，因为你知道，对我们来说去市中心是一件大事。

sentences.en: So back in 1960, when Scent of Mystery first premiered, Joan was a kid living in Chicago,
sentences.zh: 所以在1960年，《神秘的香味》首映时，琼是一个住在芝加哥的小孩，

sentences.en: and it turns out she and her siblings were part of a very small group of moviegoers
sentences.zh: 事实证明她和她的兄弟姐妹是一小群电影观众中的一员，

sentences.en: who got to see it exhibited in its full intended experience,
sentences.zh: 他们得以观看了它以完整预期的体验展映，

sentences.en: which was demonstrated by this one scene in particular.
sentences.zh: 这通过其中一个特定场景得到了展示。

sentences.en: So all of a sudden, as I'm sitting there, the main character, some chase thing is going on,
sentences.zh: 所以突然间，当我坐在那里时，主角，正在进行某种追逐戏，

sentences.en: and the main character all of a sudden goes into a flower market,
sentences.zh: 主角突然走进一个花市，

sentences.en: and this gush of sweet smell comes in our face, and neither of us can breathe.
sentences.zh: 一股甜美的气味扑面而来，我们俩都喘不过气来。

sentences.en: And of course, I had to rush over and get away from the smell.
sentences.zh: 当然，我不得不赶紧跑开，远离那种气味。

sentences.en: A gush of sweet smell.
sentences.zh: 一股甜美的气味。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what word in that phrase I find the most objectionable.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定那个短语里哪个词让我觉得最反感。

sentences.en: What kind of smell are we talking about here?
sentences.zh: 我们在这里讨论的是哪种气味？

sentences.en: So as it turns out, what Joan was experiencing in that movie theater was smell-o-vision.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，琼在那个电影院里体验到的是气味电影。

sentences.en: Roman, what do you know about smell-o-vision?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你对气味电影了解多少？

sentences.en: I mean, not much other than the name.
sentences.zh: 我是说，除了名字之外没了解多少。

sentences.en: I'm sure it has something to do with the technology that allows you to smell a movie as you're watching it.
sentences.zh: 我确信它与某种技术有关，这种技术能让你在观看电影时闻到电影里的气味。

sentences.en: But I didn't think there was much more to it than that.
sentences.zh: 但我以为事情仅此而已，没有更多了。

sentences.en: Oh, Roman, buckle up.
sentences.zh: 哦，罗曼，系好安全带。

sentences.en: It was the brainchild of American film producer Mike Todd Jr.
sentences.zh: 它是美国电影制片人小迈克·托德的心血结晶。

sentences.en: And Mike Todd Jr.
sentences.zh: 而小迈克·托德

sentences.en: was the son of, you guessed it, Mike Todd Sr.,
sentences.zh: 正如你所猜到的，他是老迈克·托德的儿子，

sentences.en: who was a hugely successful theatrical impresario and husband of Elizabeth Taylor.
sentences.zh: 老迈克·托德是一位非常成功的戏剧 impresario（戏剧经纪人/制作人）兼伊丽莎白·泰勒的丈夫。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, Mike Todd Sr.
sentences.zh: 所以，老迈克·托德

sentences.en: was this big ideas guy who loved gimmicks and doing things on a grand scale,
sentences.zh: 是一个满脑子大主意的人，喜欢噱头和大场面，

sentences.en: like his hit Oscar-winning film Around the World in 80 Days.
sentences.zh: 比如他轰动一时的奥斯卡获奖电影《环游世界80天》。

sentences.en: It was chock full of cameos and stars and, as you could guess, shot around the world.
sentences.zh: 它里面挤满了客串和明星，正如你能猜到的，是在世界各地拍摄的。

sentences.en: But then Mike Todd Sr.
sentences.zh: 但随后老迈克·托德

sentences.en: tragically died in a plane crash in 1958,
sentences.zh: 在1958年的一场飞机失事中不幸身亡，

sentences.en: leaving his son, Mike Jr., to run his production company when he was only 28 years old.
sentences.zh: 留下他的儿子小迈克在年仅28岁时经营他的制作公司。

sentences.en: And Mike Todd Jr.
sentences.zh: 而小迈克·托德

sentences.en: wanted to continue his father's legacy of spectacle.
sentences.zh: 想要延续他父亲的奇观传奇。

sentences.en: And in this moment of uncertainty, he remembered this technology that his father was intrigued by,
sentences.zh: 在这个充满不确定性的时刻，他想起了他父亲很感兴趣的这项技术，

sentences.en: and it actually considered implementing in Around the World in 80 Days,
sentences.zh: 并且实际上考虑在《环游世界80天》中应用它，

sentences.en: this thing called smell brain.
sentences.zh: 这个被称为“气味大脑”的东西。

sentences.en: That needs some work.
sentences.zh: 这名字需要改进一下。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: So, smell brain was this device invented by an Austrian osmologist named Hans Lobb.
sentences.zh: 所以，“气味大脑”是由一位名叫汉斯·洛布的奥地利气味学家发明的设备。

sentences.en: And it was essentially a conveyor belt full of vials containing smell cues.
sentences.zh: 它本质上是一个装满包含气味线索的小瓶的传送带。

sentences.en: And when prompted, the smell brain would pump the scent cue to each seat in the theater individually using a series of tubes.
sentences.zh: 当收到提示时，“气味大脑”会通过一系列管道将气味线索单独输送到剧院的每个座位。

sentences.en: So, it was like this synced smell experience matching what was on the screen.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像是一种与银幕内容相匹配的同步气味体验。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Mike Todd Jr.
sentences.zh: 小迈克·托德

sentences.en: remembered the smell brain and Lobb and thought,
sentences.zh: 想起了“气味大脑”和洛布，然后心想，

sentences.en: okay, I'm going to invest all of my money and the resources from my dad's production company
sentences.zh: 好吧，我要投入我所有的钱和我爸爸制作公司的资源，

sentences.en: because what moviegoers really want is to smell the movies.
sentences.zh: 因为电影观众真正想要的是闻到电影的气味。

sentences.en: And this is with no market testing to support it,
sentences.zh: 而且这没有任何市场测试来支持它，

sentences.en: just the firm belief people would be so excited by the idea of sniffing stuff while watching a movie
sentences.zh: 仅仅是一种坚定的信念，人们会因为在看电影时闻东西这个想法而如此兴奋，

sentences.en: that they would rush to theaters.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们会蜂拥至电影院。

sentences.en: Well, history is made by dreamers, so go for it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，历史是由梦想家创造的，所以放手去做吧。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: So, Mike Todd, he's a marketing guy.
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克·托德，他是个营销人员。

sentences.en: So, he decides to rebrand smell brain with a more attention-grabbing name,
sentences.zh: 因此，他决定用一个更吸引眼球的名字来重新包装“气味大脑”，

sentences.en: Smell-O-Vision.
sentences.zh: 也就是“气味电影”（Smell-O-Vision）。

sentences.en: And he decided the way to debut this Smell-O-Vision technology
sentences.zh: 他决定推出这项“气味电影”技术的方式

sentences.en: was to produce and self-finance the first and only film made with the smell cues in mind during production,
sentences.zh: 是制作并自行资助第一部也是唯一一部在制作过程中考虑到气味线索的电影，

sentences.en: Scent of Mystery.
sentences.zh: 《神秘的香味》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The title is extremely on the nose.
sentences.zh: 这个片名极其直白。

sentences.en: Bah, bah.
sentences.zh: 哈哈。

sentences.en: Oh, sorry.
sentences.zh: 哦，抱歉。

sentences.en: I actually didn't mean that.
sentences.zh: 我其实不是那个意思。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, what was different about the film Scent of Mystery from other films?
sentences.zh: 那么电影《神秘的香味》与其他电影有什么不同？

sentences.en: Like, how did it showcase the Smell-O-Vision technology?
sentences.zh: 比如说，它是如何展示“气味电影”技术的？

sentences.en: Oh, so, deploying scents in the movie-watching experience actually goes as far back as the silent era.
sentences.zh: 哦，所以，在观影体验中运用气味其实可以追溯到无声电影时代。

sentences.en: So, maybe a theater would show a film that had a scene at the Rose Bowl,
sentences.zh: 所以，也许一家影院会放映一部在玫瑰碗体育场有一个场景的电影，

sentences.en: and the theater owner would put a cotton ball soaked with rose oil in front of a fan to enhance that experience for the audience.
sentences.zh: 影院老板会在风扇前面放一个浸有玫瑰油的棉球，以增强观众的体验。

sentences.en: So, some audiences got to experience the smell of movies before they even heard them.
sentences.zh: 所以一些观众在听到电影声音之前就体验到了电影的气味。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But in those pre-Smell-O-Vision experiences, the smell cues were created by the theater owners and not necessarily how the filmmaker intended the movie to be experienced.
sentences.zh: 但在那些“气味电影”之前的体验中，气味线索是由影院老板创造的，不一定符合电影制作人原本希望观众体验电影的方式。

sentences.en: Smell-O-Vision and Scent of Mystery were going to be different because it was the first time the scents were going to be intentionally embedded into the production of the film,
sentences.zh: “气味电影”和《神秘的香味》将会有所不同，因为这是气味第一次被有意地嵌入到电影的制作中，

sentences.en: and the smells would be critical to the plot.
sentences.zh: 并且这些气味对于剧情至关重要。

sentences.en: So, how does a smell-driven plot even work?
sentences.zh: 那么，以气味为主导的剧情到底是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, like I mentioned before, there is a mysterious woman character, and everyone's trying to figure out who this mysterious woman is.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像我之前提到的，有一个神秘的女性角色，每个人都试图弄清楚这个神秘女性是谁。

sentences.en: And every time you see this mysterious woman, you would smell her perfume.
sentences.zh: 而且每次你看到这个神秘女性，你都会闻到她的香水味。

sentences.en: So, the smell of the perfume was pumped into the audience, and then that smell is key to figuring out her identity.
sentences.zh: 所以，香水的味道被输送到观众席中，然后这种味道是弄清她身份的关键。

sentences.en: And you thought there might have been one other.
sentences.zh: 你以为可能还有另一个。

sentences.en: Una otra.
sentences.zh: 另一个。

sentences.en: She buy perfume.
sentences.zh: 她买香水。

sentences.en: Scent of mystery.
sentences.zh: 神秘的香味。

sentences.en: Magnifico.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Irresistible.
sentences.zh: 无法抗拒。

sentences.en: In that scene that you just heard, you would actually smell the perfume that you saw on screen.
sentences.zh: 在你刚听到的那个场景里，你实际上能闻到银幕上看到的香水味。

sentences.en: But, dear listeners, you're just going to have to use your imagination.
sentences.zh: 但是，亲爱的听众们，你们只能发挥你们的想象力了。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: So, Mike Dodd Jr.
sentences.zh: 所以，小迈克·多德

sentences.en: was so convinced that Smell-O-Vision was going to revolutionize cinema that he marketed it as a seismic advancement.
sentences.zh: 深信气味电影将彻底改变电影界，于是将其作为一项轰动的进步进行营销。
